articles.title: Seventeen Years After Her First Match in England, Harmanpreet Kaur Walked Out for Her 200th — a Number No Cricketer Had Ever Reached
articles.excerpt: India's captain became the first player, man or woman, to appear in 200 T20 Internationals. That it happened at a World Cup in the same country where she debuted as a teenager in 2009 made the milestone read like a story written in advance.
articles.image_caption: Harmanpreet Kaur, India's captain and the first cricketer to play 200 T20 Internationals
articles.nri_angle: Harmanpreet Kaur is one of the players through whom the Indian diaspora embraced the women's game, and her 17-year climb to a record 200 T20Is mirrors the rise of women's cricket in India that NRIs have followed with growing pride — a story of persistence rewarded that resonates across a community built on long journeys far from home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Most Famous Paddler Missed the Asian Games Team by One Ranking Place
articles.excerpt: Manika Batra, the face of Indian table tennis, has been named only a reserve: world No. 51, one spot short of the top-50 ranking that would have guaranteed her a place. Her public appeal to the Prime Minister has reopened an old fight over how India picks its athletes.
articles.image_caption: Manika Batra receiving the Arjuna Award in 2018
articles.nri_angle: Manika Batra is one of the few Indian Olympic-sport athletes with genuine global recognition, and the row over whether a transparent ranking rule should override proven international pedigree strikes a familiar chord with NRIs who follow India's Olympic-sport rise and value merit-based process.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Europe Just Launched Its First Big-League T20 — and the Diaspora Built Half the Talent Pool
articles.excerpt: The ICC-sanctioned European T20 Premier League opened its player draft this week, with six city franchises across Ireland, Scotland and the Netherlands — cricketing nations whose teams the South Asian diaspora has quietly powered for years.
articles.image_caption: Malahide Cricket Ground in Dublin, one of Ireland's international venues; the new ETPL will field two Irish franchises, in Dublin and Belfast
articles.nri_angle: The Irish, Scottish and Dutch national teams the ETPL is built to strengthen have for years been substantially powered by South Asian immigrant communities, and a serious, well-broadcast home league gives diaspora families across Britain, Ireland and the Netherlands a top-tier local team to watch and a real professional pathway for their children.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Smaller India Heads to Glasgow — and the Sports It Wins Most Aren't on the Bill
articles.excerpt: India will send just 125-130 athletes and staff to a stripped-down Commonwealth Games that has dropped wrestling, badminton, hockey and table tennis — its richest medal seams.
articles.image_caption: Weightlifter Mirabai Chanu, one of India's medal hopes in a Glasgow programme that retains weightlifting
articles.nri_angle: The Commonwealth Games have long been the most accessible stage for Indians in Britain, Canada and Australia to watch their country compete, and Glasgow's stripped-down programme — minus India's signature sports of badminton, wrestling and hockey — means fewer of those moments, even as Ahmedabad's 2030 Games promise to bring the event home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Unbeaten Run Ends at Old Trafford, Undone by a Marizanne Kapp Masterclass
articles.excerpt: Chasing 159, South Africa rode an unbeaten 81 from Marizanne Kapp to beat India by six wickets in Manchester, handing the tournament favourites their first defeat of the Women's T20 World Cup.
articles.image_caption: Marizanne Kapp, whose unbeaten 81 powered South Africa past India at Old Trafford
articles.nri_angle: India's women had built a genuine diaspora following on the back of an unbeaten World Cup start, and this first defeat — in front of a large Indian community in Manchester and over breakfast tables across the US — is the moment that romance met a colder reality, with semifinal seeding now on the line.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Women Won in Auckland, and With It a Ticket Back to the Top Table of World Hockey
articles.excerpt: India beat hosts New Zealand 2-0 to lift the FIH Women's Nations Cup and seal promotion to the Pro League, a year after being relegated from the same elite tier.
articles.image_caption: India goalkeeper Savita, whose side beat New Zealand to win the FIH Women's Nations Cup in Auckland (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: A year after India's women were relegated from world hockey's elite Pro League, an unbeaten Nations Cup run and a final won on New Zealand soil sends them back to the top tier — a redemption arc that resonates with NRI families from London to Toronto to Auckland, where the final was staged in front of a large local Indian community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kohli Is Coming Back to England — This Time With a White Ball, and the Diaspora Is Counting Down
articles.excerpt: India recalled Virat Kohli for next month's three ODIs in England, subject to a fitness test. Yashasvi Jaiswal, who replaced him and made a hundred against Afghanistan, was left out.
articles.image_caption: Virat Kohli, recalled to India's ODI squad for the July tour of England, subject to a fitness test
articles.nri_angle: No cricketer moves tickets and travel plans across Britain like Virat Kohli, and his recall means the UK's vast NRI community can watch him at Edgbaston, Cardiff and Lord's in July — a homecoming of sorts staged thousands of miles from home, in the same English summer India began their Test era without him.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Two Hundreds, 460 Runs, One Game: America's Cricket League Just Staged Its Most Brutal Run-Fest Yet
articles.excerpt: Mitchell Owen smashed 155 and Kieron Pollard answered with an unbeaten 100, but Washington Freedom's 245 was 30 too many for MI New York at Grand Prairie.
articles.image_caption: Kieron Pollard, who struck an unbeaten 100 off 56 balls for MI New York at Grand Prairie
articles.nri_angle: MLC was sold to the NRI community as world-class T20 cricket in their own time zone and backyard — and a match where both Mitchell Owen and Kieron Pollard score hundreds, with US international Saurabh Netravalkar in the home XI, is that promise delivered for the diaspora that built American cricket's heartland in suburbs like Grand Prairie.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Samurai Blue Surge: Japan Dominates Tunisia in Monterrey Showpiece
articles.excerpt: Japan's emphatic 4-0 victory over Tunisia reshapes Group F dynamics.
articles.image_caption: Estadio BBVA in Monterrey — venue for Tunisia vs Japan at the 2026 FIFA World Cup (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: The Indian-American community, pivotal in North America, added vibrancy and support to the match in Monterrey, illustrating football's unifying power.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: On the First Day of the Post-Kohli Era, Two Centuries Said India Will Be Just Fine
articles.excerpt: Shubman Gill marked his first Test as captain with an unbeaten 127, Yashasvi Jaiswal made 101 on his maiden innings in England, and India closed Headingley's opening day on 359 for three.
articles.image_caption: India captain Shubman Gill, who made an unbeaten 127 on his Test captaincy debut at Headingley (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Day 1 at Headingley was the first real look at Indian Test cricket without Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma — and for NRI families who plan summers around the England tour and measure home through this team, twin centuries from a new captain and a young opener were the most reassuring start the post-Kohli era could have offered.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: San Francisco Bounced Back in Texas, and an Indian-American Was There at the Finish
articles.excerpt: Lhuan-dre Pretorius anchored the Unicorns' seven-wicket win over the Texas Super Kings with an unbeaten 69, while Sanjay Krishnamurthy closed it out and R. Ashwin watched on from a star-studded SF squad.
articles.image_caption: Ravichandran Ashwin, the India spin great who is part of the San Francisco Unicorns squad in MLC 2026
articles.nri_angle: The San Francisco Unicorns squad features India spin legend R. Ashwin, and Indian-American Sanjay Krishnamurthy finished the winning chase — in a league played in the Bay Area and Texas suburbs the Indian and South Asian diaspora calls home, and which their support has underwritten from the start.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Seattle Chased 217 in Texas and Barely Broke Stride. America's T20 League Is Producing Run-Fests the Diaspora Built It For.
articles.excerpt: Tim Seifert's 78 off 33 and Matthew Breetzke's 66 powered the Orcas past Washington Freedom by five wickets with 14 balls to spare, the latest blockbuster in a Major League Cricket season the NRI suburbs made possible.
articles.image_caption: Glenn Maxwell of Washington Freedom during the 2026 Major League Cricket season
articles.nri_angle: Major League Cricket is played in the very North American suburbs the Indian and South Asian diaspora calls home, and features USA internationals of Indian origin like Saurabh Netravalkar — making the league's run-fests a proof of concept for cricket's permanent roots in America ahead of the LA 2028 Olympics.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jaiswal's Unbeaten 110 Seals a 3-0 Sweep — and the First Clean Verdict on India's Post-Kohli ODI Team
articles.excerpt: India brushed Afghanistan aside by nine wickets in Chennai to complete a whitewash, but the real story is a new-look side under Shubman Gill building quietly toward the 2027 World Cup.
articles.image_caption: Yashasvi Jaiswal, whose unbeaten 110 sealed India's 3-0 ODI series sweep of Afghanistan in Chennai
articles.nri_angle: The Afghanistan sweep is the first full look at India's post-Kohli ODI side under new captain Shubman Gill, whose names — Jaiswal, Kishan, Prasidh Krishna — will headline the white-ball tours bringing India to grounds across North America and England in the years ahead.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Has Never Played a World Cup. On Sunday in Vancouver, a Punjabi From Auckland Carries Its Hopes Anyway.
articles.excerpt: Sarpreet Singh, whose parents left Jalandhar for New Zealand, has become the first Sikh footballer to play at a World Cup — and the Kiwis' must-win clash with Egypt is now appointment viewing for the diaspora.
articles.image_caption: Sarpreet Singh, the New Zealand midfielder of Punjabi heritage who has become the first Sikh footballer to play at a World Cup
articles.nri_angle: India have never played a men's World Cup, but Sarpreet Singh — an Auckland-born midfielder whose parents emigrated from Jalandhar, Punjab — has become the first Sikh footballer to play at one, and his New Zealand side's must-win clash with Egypt makes the tournament personal for South Asian fans across North America.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Two Indian-Americans Made the U.S. Open Weekend. Three Recent Champions Did Not.
articles.excerpt: As Bryson DeChambeau, Jon Rahm and Brooks Koepka were sent home from Shinnecock Hills, Sahith Theegala and Akshay Bhatia survived the brutal cut — with Theegala sitting inside the top 10 heading into Moving Day.
articles.image_caption: Akshay Bhatia, who made the cut at the 2026 U.S. Open at Shinnecock Hills
articles.nri_angle: Sahith Theegala and Akshay Bhatia, both American golfers of Indian descent, made the weekend cut at the 2026 U.S. Open while recent major champions were eliminated — a marker of the deepening Indian-American presence in a sport where the diaspora has historically had little visibility.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Bay Area's Team Began Its Season 117 for 2 — and Still Lost. The Unicorns' Collapse Handed LA the Opener.
articles.excerpt: San Francisco Unicorns slipped from a commanding position to 150 for 7 in a rain-shortened game, and Colin Munro's unbeaten 64 made the Knight Riders' chase look routine as Major League Cricket's fourth season began at Grand Prairie.
articles.image_caption: Colin Munro, whose unbeaten 64 carried the LA Knight Riders past the San Francisco Unicorns
articles.nri_angle: The San Francisco Unicorns are the Bay Area's home franchise — backed by Indian-American tech entrepreneurs and embraced by one of the densest South Asian communities in the US — making their MLC season opener a marquee event for a diaspora watching cricket take root in America.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Six Goals, Zero Conceded: India's Women Storm Into the Nations Cup Final — and to the Brink of the Pro League
articles.excerpt: A 6-0 demolition of Chile in Auckland puts the Indian women's hockey team one win from the trophy and, more importantly, from a return to the elite FIH Pro League they were relegated from last year.
articles.image_caption: India women's hockey captain Salima Tete, who led the side to the Nations Cup final
articles.nri_angle: Played in a New Zealand time zone that suits NRI viewers and streamed free online, India's women are one win from a return to hockey's elite Pro League — a milestone the diaspora can watch live as the programme rebuilds toward the 2028 LA Olympics.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Paraguay’s Tenacious Triumph in San Francisco Seals Turkey’s Fate
articles.excerpt: Paraguay triumphs over Turkey with an early goal, securing a 1-0 win despite playing with ten men.
articles.image_caption: Levi's Stadium in San Francisco Bay Area — venue for Turkey vs Paraguay at the 2026 FIFA World Cup (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: The match was a cultural celebration, reflecting the diverse, multicultural community of the Bay Area, home to a large Indian-American population.

articles.title: He Is 15, He Broke the IPL's Records, and Now India Are Sending His Parents With Him to Watch His Debut
articles.excerpt: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's maiden call-up for the white-ball tour of Ireland and England makes him one of the youngest cricketers India has ever picked — and the BCCI is taking the unusual step of flying his parents along to ease a schoolboy into an adult dressing room.
articles.image_caption: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, the 15-year-old handed a maiden India T20I call-up
articles.nri_angle: The most-hyped teenager in world cricket will make his India debut on the diaspora's doorstep — in Belfast and across England — letting British-Indian families watch the sport's next superstar in person rather than on a screen half a world away.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: New Captain, New Trophy, New Era: India Begin in England Without Rohit and Kohli for the First Time in a Generation
articles.excerpt: When the first ball is bowled at Headingley on Saturday, it will open the Anderson-Tendulkar Trophy, the 2025-27 World Test Championship, and the captaincy of 25-year-old Shubman Gill — with the two batters who defined Indian cricket for 15 years watching from home.
articles.image_caption: Shubman Gill, who leads India in his first Test as captain at Headingley
articles.nri_angle: An India tour of England is a fixed point on the British-Indian calendar, filling Headingley, Lord's and Edgbaston with travelling support — and this summer the diaspora gets its first sustained look at the post-Rohit, post-Kohli team under a new captain, playing for a trophy now bearing Sachin Tendulkar's name.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Neeraj Chopra Finished Fourth on His Comeback. The Number That Matters Is 85.69.
articles.excerpt: After 275 days out with a back injury, India's two-time Olympic medallist returned in Doha well short of his best — but his season's-best throw cleared the Commonwealth Games qualifying mark, and that was the point all along.
articles.image_caption: Neeraj Chopra, who returned from a back injury to finish fourth at the 2026 Doha Diamond League
articles.nri_angle: Neeraj Chopra is the rare Indian track-and-field superstar the diaspora has made appointment viewing, and his healthy return from a long injury lay-off — with a Commonwealth Games berth already secured — keeps alive the medal hopes NRIs rally behind at every global championship.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An Ankle Twisted in the Powerplay Ended One World Cup. It Began Another for an Uncapped Spinner Who Was Already in England.
articles.excerpt: Shreyanka Patil is out of the Women's T20 World Cup after injuring her ankle against the Netherlands. Her replacement, 24-year-old legspinner Prema Rawat, has never played for India — and got the call while on an India A tour bus in England.
articles.image_caption: India's women's cricket team with the 2025 Women's Cricket World Cup trophy
articles.nri_angle: India's women's cricket team became a unifying obsession for NRIs after the 2025 50-over World Cup title, and the squad's depth — an uncapped spinner stepping in for an injured star without missing a beat — is exactly the kind of story the diaspora rallies behind as the team chases its first T20 World Cup.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: He Was Born in Paris, His Mother Is Congolese, and His Tamil Roots Run Through a Caribbean Island. Meet the Fourth Indian at This World Cup.
articles.excerpt: Samuel Moutoussamy played all 90 minutes of DR Congo's 1-1 draw with Portugal in Houston — the least-known of the four players carrying Indian heritage onto the 2026 World Cup stage, and the one with the longest, strangest journey home to it.
articles.image_caption: DR Congo midfielder Samuel Moutoussamy, of Tamil-Guadeloupean and Congolese descent, one of four players of Indian origin at the 2026 World Cup
articles.nri_angle: Samuel Moutoussamy is the fourth and least-known player of Indian descent at the 2026 World Cup — and the one with the deepest diaspora thread, tracing his Tamil roots to 19th-century indentured migrants in the French Caribbean island of Guadeloupe. For a diaspora that has never seen India reach a World Cup, he is an unlikely point of connection, and his June 27 group game against Uzbekistan in Atlanta will be within reach of America's South Asian community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Two From Two, and the One Trophy They've Never Won Looks Closer Than Ever
articles.excerpt: India's women, reigning 50-over world champions, have opened the T20 World Cup in England with a 64-run rout of Pakistan and a record-breaking 95-run demolition of the Netherlands — and a diaspora that has waited a generation for this is watching.
articles.image_caption: India vice-captain Smriti Mandhana, whose back-to-back player-of-the-match displays have anchored India's unbeaten start to the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup
articles.nri_angle: India's women, reigning 50-over world champions, are chasing the one global title that has always eluded them — and a diaspora across England, the US and Canada is watching, in stadiums in Birmingham, Leeds and Manchester or on JioHotstar streams at all hours. After last year's home-soil ODI breakthrough, an unbeaten T20 World Cup start has given a generation of NRI fans permission to dream of a first T20 crown.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
